page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity, storage-optimized server in the Lasv4 instance family designed for compute- and I/O-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, this server supplies 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The hardware includes 768 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 23,038 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Architectural instruction support covers AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark analysis highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing capability, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 147,596.42, a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,976.0, and a PassMark CPU rating of 92,661.83. Memory performance features a top-tier small-block bandwidth of 7,287.47 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 229.38 GB/sec and writes achieve 140.83 GB/sec. Application benchmarks show top-tier throughput in key operational tasks, generating 122.77 million Redis SET operations per second and executing bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 547.27 GB/sec.

The integration of massive direct-attached NVMe storage alongside 768 GB of system memory provides elevated qualitative cost efficiency by removing reliance on expensive external block storage arrays for high-IOPS applications. Consolidating storage-dense operations onto a single node reduces network latency and architectural complexity. Recommended workload fits include enterprise relational and NoSQL databases, high-performance in-memory key-value stores like Redis, software compilation, big data analytics, and CPU-driven LLM prompt processing.
